lab_title: Visualizing Vector Operations and Projectile Motion in AR
top_level_objectives: Define vectors through magnitude and direction and master tip-to-tail addition.
Decompose vectors into x and y components using trigonometric principles.
Demonstrate that horizontal and vertical motion in projectiles are independent.
Predict how changes in launch velocity and angle affect range and height.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce vectors as objects with magnitude and direction in 3D space.
key_visuals: Two interactive 3D arrows representing force or velocity vectors.
Floating numerical readouts for magnitude and angle.
student_actions: Grab and rotate vectors to observe changes in direction.
Adjust the length of the arrows to change magnitude.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the tip-to-tail addition method to find a resultant vector.
key_visuals: A ghost-image of a resultant vector appearing automatically when vectors are connected.
Visual guides showing the 'tip' and 'tail' alignment.
student_actions: Drag one vector so its tail touches the tip of the other.
Observe how the resultant vector updates in real-time.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the decomposition of a vector into its orthogonal components.
key_visuals: Dashed projection lines falling onto x and y axes.
A right-triangle overlay showing the vector as the hypotenuse.
student_actions: Slide a vector along the plane to see how components change dynamically.
Toggle between the raw vector and its horizontal/vertical components.

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to an initial velocity vector for a projectile.
key_visuals: A launching cannon platform at the origin.
The initial velocity vector showing horizontal and vertical components.
student_actions: Change the launch angle to see how the relative size of x and y components changes.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show the independence of horizontal and vertical motion components.
key_visuals: Color-coded 'velocity trails' (one for horizontal speed, one for vertical speed).
student_actions: Watch the projectile move; notice the horizontal component's constant length versus the vertical component's changing length.

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect component behavior to the resulting parabolic path.
key_visuals: A persistent arc showing the full trajectory.
Ghost copies of the projectile dropping straight down from its horizontal position.
student_actions: Trace the projectile path and see how it is built by the independent x and y motions.

scenes.brief_purpose: Synthesize learning by optimizing projectile flight parameters.
key_visuals: A virtual target placed at a specific range.
Controls for launch velocity and angle.
student_actions: Adjust launch angle and speed to successfully hit the target.
Analyze why specific settings yield different heights and distances.
